description: This circular chart visually organizes medical ethics principles into four main categories—Beneficence, Justice, Non-Maleficence, and Autonomy—each represented by a distinct colored segment at the center of the wheel. The largest segment, Beneficence, is blue and contains the most subcategories, including “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” and “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” among others. The Justice segment is orange and includes principles like “Promote Environmental Sustainability,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” and “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally.” The Non-Maleficence segment is purple and lists duties such as “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care,” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain.” The Autonomy segment is green and encompasses rights including “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve,” “Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement,” and “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed, Freedom of Choice.” Each of these main categories is further subdivided into numerous smaller, text-labeled slices radiating outward from the central circle, with no explicit percentage values shown inside the slices. The chart does not include a legend or percentage labels within the slices, though the relative sizes of the main categories suggest Beneficence is the largest, followed by Autonomy, then Justice, and Non-Maleficence being the smallest. The segments appear to be arranged in a clockwise order around the central circle, with the largest category occupying roughly half the circle’s circumference.
